sanskrit: kṛśa uvāca sa rājā mṛgayāṃ yātaḥ parikṣid abhimanyujaḥ sasāra mṛgam ekākī viddhvā bāṇena patriṇā
english: Kṛśa said: That king Parīkṣit, son of Abhimanyu, having gone out hunting, chased a deer alone after wounding it with a feathered arrow.

sanskrit: na cāpaśyan mṛgaṃ rājā caraṃs tasmin mahāvane pitaraṃ te sa dṛṣṭvaiva papracchānabhibhāṣiṇam
english: Not finding the deer as he roamed that great forest, the king, upon seeing your father, questioned him — though he was one who did not speak.

sanskrit: taṃ sthāṇubhūtaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ kṣutpipāsāśramāturaḥ punaḥ punar mṛgaṃ naṣṭaṃ papraccha pitaraṃ tava
english: Him standing there motionless as a post, the king — exhausted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue — questioned your father again and again about the lost deer.

sanskrit: sa ca maunavratopeto naiva taṃ pratyabhāṣata tasya rājā dhanuṣkoṭyā sarpaṃ skandhe samāsṛjat
english: But he, bound by his vow of silence, did not answer him at all; and the king, with the tip of his bow, placed a dead serpent upon his shoulder.

sanskrit: śṛṅgiṃs tava pitādyāsau tathaivāste yatavrataḥ so 'pi rājā svanagaraṃ pratiyāto gajāhvayam
english: O Śṛṅgin, your father sits just so even now, steadfast in his vow; and that king has returned to his own city, Gajāhvaya.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śrutvaivam ṛṣiputras tu divaṃ stabdhveva viṣṭhitaḥ kopasaṃraktanayanaḥ prajvalann iva manyunā
english: The Sūta said: Hearing this, the son of the sage stood as though he had struck the sky, his eyes red with rage, blazing as it were with wrath.

sanskrit: āviṣṭaḥ sa tu kopena śaśāpa nṛpatiṃ tadā vāry upaspṛśya tejasvī krodhavegabalātkṛtaḥ
english: Seized by anger, that brilliant one then cursed the king, touching water and overpowered by the force and violence of his fury.

sanskrit: śṛṅgy uvāca yo 'sau vṛddhasya tātasya tathā kṛcchragatasya ca skandhe mṛtam avāsrākṣīt pannagaṃ rājakilbiṣī
english: Śṛṅgin said: That sinful king who has thrown a dead serpent upon the shoulder of my aged father while he was in distress —

sanskrit: taṃ pāpam atisaṃkruddhas takṣakaḥ pannagottamaḥ āśīviṣas tigmatejā madvākyabalacoditaḥ
english: — that wicked one, Takṣaka the foremost of serpents, venomous-fanged, of fierce brilliance, urged on by the power of my words in great fury,

sanskrit: saptarātrādito netā yamasya sadanaṃ prati dvijānām avamantāraṃ kurūṇām ayaśaskaram
english: shall conduct him from this day to the abode of Yama within seven nights — this despiser of brahmins, this disgrace to the Kurus.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca iti śaptvā nṛpaṃ kruddhaḥ śṛṅgī pitaram abhyayāt āsīnaṃ gocare tasmin vahantaṃ śavapannagam
english: The Sūta said: Having thus cursed the king in his anger, Śṛṅgin went to his father, who sat in that grove still bearing the dead serpent.

sanskrit: sa tam ālakṣya pitaraṃ śṛṅgī skandhagatena vai śavena bhujagenāsīd bhūyaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ
english: Seeing his father with the dead serpent still upon his shoulder, Śṛṅgin was filled with grief and anger anew.

sanskrit: duḥkhāc cāśrūṇi mumuce pitaraṃ cedam abravīt śrutvemāṃ dharṣaṇāṃ tāta tava tena durātmanā
english: From grief he shed tears and spoke these words to his father: "Father, having heard of this insult inflicted upon you by that wicked one —

sanskrit: rājñā parikṣitā kopād aśapaṃ tam ahaṃ nṛpam yathārhati sa evograṃ śāpaṃ kurukulādhamaḥ
english: — by King Parīkṣit, I have in my fury cursed that king with the terrible curse he deserves, the lowest of the Kuru line.

sanskrit: saptame 'hani taṃ pāpaṃ takṣakaḥ pannagottamaḥ vaivasvatasya bhavanaṃ netā paramadāruṇam
english: On the seventh day, Takṣaka, the foremost of serpents, shall conduct that wretch to the dreadful abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: tam abravīt pitā brahmaṃs tathā kopasamanvitam na me priyaṃ kṛtaṃ tāta naiṣa dharmas tapasvinām
english: His father addressed him, so filled with anger, and said: O brahmin, you have not done what is pleasing to me, my son; this is not the dharma of ascetics.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tasya narendrasya viṣaye nivasāmahe nyāyato rakṣitās tena tasya pāpaṃ na rocaye
english: We dwell in the realm of that king; we are properly protected by him. Therefore I do not approve of his being harmed.

sanskrit: sarvathā vartamānasya rājño hy asmadvidhaiḥ sadā kṣantavyaṃ putra dharmo hi hato hanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: For such as we are, we must always forgive a king acting in any manner, my son — for dharma when destroyed destroys in return; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi rājā na rakṣeta pīḍā vai naḥ parā bhavet na śaknuyāma carituṃ dharmaṃ putra yathāsukham
english: If the king did not protect us, we would suffer greatly; we would not be able to practise dharma in peace and comfort, my son.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇā vayaṃ tāta rājabhiḥ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ carāmo vipulaṃ dharmaṃ teṣāṃ cāṃśo 'sti dharmataḥ
english: Being protected by kings who act according to the scriptures, we practise abundant dharma, and they too receive a rightful share of that dharma.

sanskrit: parikṣit tu viśeṣeṇa yathāsya prapitāmahaḥ rakṣaty asmān yathā rājñā rakṣitavyāḥ prajās tathā
english: Parīkṣit in particular protects us even as his great-grandfather did; he protects his subjects as a king ought to protect them.

sanskrit: teneha kṣudhitenādya śrāntena ca tapasvinā ajānatā vratam idaṃ kṛtam etad asaṃśayam
english: By him — wearied today, hungry and fatigued, an ascetic — this was done without knowing my vow. Of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tasmād idaṃ tvayā bālyāt sahasā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam na hy arhati nṛpaḥ śāpam asmattaḥ putra sarvathā
english: Therefore this wrong act has been rashly committed by you out of childishness; for the king in no way deserves a curse from us, my son.

sanskrit: śṛṅgy uvāca yady etat sāhasaṃ tāta yadi vā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam priyaṃ vāpy apriyaṃ vā te vāg uktā na mṛṣā mayā
english: Śṛṅgin said: Whether this was rashness, father, or a wrong deed done, whether it pleases you or not — the word I have spoken is not false.

sanskrit: naivānyathedaṃ bhavitā pitar eṣa bravīmi te nāhaṃ mṛṣā prabravīmi svaireṣv api kutaḥ śapan
english: It shall not be otherwise, father — this I tell you. I do not speak falsehood even in jest; how much less when pronouncing a curse.

sanskrit: śamīka uvāca jānāmy ugraprabhāvaṃ tvāṃ putra satyagiraṃ tathā nānṛtaṃ hy uktapūrvaṃ te naitan mithyā bhaviṣyati
english: Śamīka said: I know you, my son, to be of fierce power and true speech; you have never spoken what is untrue — this too shall not prove false.

sanskrit: pitrā putro vayaḥstho 'pi satataṃ vācya eva tu yathā syād guṇasaṃyuktaḥ prāpnuyāc ca mahad yaśaḥ
english: Nevertheless, a son, however grown, must always be instructed by his father, so that he may become endowed with virtues and attain great fame.

sanskrit: kiṃ punar bāla eva tvaṃ tapasā bhāvitaḥ prabho vardhate ca prabhavatāṃ kopo 'tīva mahātmanām
english: How much more so when you are but a child, though formed by asceticism, O lord. And indeed the anger of great souls who are powerful grows exceedingly.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ paśyāmi vaktavyaṃ tvayi dharmabhṛtāṃ vara putratvaṃ bālatāṃ caiva tavāvekṣya ca sāhasam
english: So I see that you, O best upholder of dharma, must be spoken to, considering both your filial status and your youth, as well as this rashness of yours.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ śamayuto bhūtvā vanyam āhāram āharan cara krodham imaṃ tyaktvā naivaṃ dharmaṃ prahāsyasi
english: Therefore, be possessed of calmness, live subsisting on forest food, and abandon this anger — do not thus forsake dharma.

sanskrit: krodho hi dharmaṃ harati yatīnāṃ duḥkhasaṃcitam tato dharmavihīnānāṃ gatir iṣṭā na vidyate
english: For anger destroys the dharma that ascetics have accumulated through suffering; and those bereft of dharma do not attain the desired goal.

sanskrit: śama eva yatīnāṃ hi kṣamiṇāṃ siddhikārakaḥ kṣamāvatām ayaṃ lokaḥ paraś caiva kṣamāvatām
english: Serenity alone is the cause of perfection for ascetics who possess forbearance; both this world and the next belong to those endowed with forbearance.

sanskrit: tasmāc carethāḥ satataṃ kṣamāśīlo jitendriyaḥ kṣamayā prāpsyase lokān brahmaṇaḥ samanantarān
english: Therefore conduct yourself always with forbearance as your nature, with senses conquered; through forbearance you shall attain worlds next to that of Brahman.

sanskrit: mayā tu śamam āsthāya yac chakyaṃ kartum adya vai tat kariṣye 'dya tātāhaṃ preṣayiṣye nṛpāya vai
english: But I, resorting to calmness, shall do what can be done today — I shall send a messenger to the king this very day.

sanskrit: mama putreṇa śapto 'si bālenākṛtabuddhinā mamemāṃ dharṣaṇāṃ tvattaḥ prekṣya rājann amarṣiṇā
english: "You have been cursed by my son, a child of immature understanding, O king, who was provoked to indignation upon witnessing this insult to me inflicted by you."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evamādiśya śiṣyaṃ sa preṣayām āsa suvrataḥ parikṣite nṛpataye dayāpanno mahātapāḥ
english: The Sūta said: Having given these instructions to his disciple, that great ascetic of good vows, moved by compassion, sent him to King Parīkṣit.

sanskrit: saṃdiśya kuśalapraśnaṃ kāryavṛttāntam eva ca śiṣyaṃ gauramukhaṃ nāma śīlavantaṃ samāhitam
english: Having enjoined him to convey greetings and also to recount the entire matter, he sent the disciple named Gauramukha, a virtuous and composed man.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya tataḥ śīghraṃ narendraṃ kuruvardhanam viveśa bhavanaṃ rājñaḥ pūrvaṃ dvāḥsthair niveditaḥ
english: Quickly approaching the king, the enhancer of the Kuru line, and first being announced by the doorkeepers, he entered the royal palace.

sanskrit: pūjitaś ca narendreṇa dvijo gauramukhas tataḥ ācakhyau pariviśrānto rājñe sarvam aśeṣataḥ śamīkavacanaṃ ghoraṃ yathoktaṃ mantrisaṃnidhau
english: After being duly honoured by the king, the brahmin Gauramukha, having rested, related everything in full to the king — the terrible message of Śamīka just as it was spoken — in the presence of the ministers.

sanskrit: śamīko nāma rājendra viṣaye vartate tava ṛṣiḥ paramadharmātmā dāntaḥ śānto mahātapāḥ
english: "There lives in your realm, O king of kings, a sage named Śamīka — one of supreme righteous soul, self-restrained, calm, and of great austerity.

sanskrit: tasya tvayā naravyāghra sarpaḥ prāṇair viyojitaḥ avasakto dhanuṣkoṭyā skandhe bharatasattama kṣāntavāṃs tava tat karma putras tasya na cakṣame
english: O tiger among men, O best of the Bhāratas, a serpent robbed of life was placed by you on his shoulder with the tip of your bow. He himself forgave your act, but his son could not endure it.

sanskrit: tena śapto 'si rājendra pitur ajñātam adya vai takṣakaḥ saptarātreṇa mṛtyus te vai bhaviṣyati
english: You have been cursed by him, O king, without his father's knowledge: Takṣaka shall be your death within seven nights.

sanskrit: tatra rakṣāṃ kuruṣveti punaḥ punar athābravīt tad anyathā na śakyaṃ ca kartuṃ kena cid apy uta
english: 'Protect yourself in this matter,' he said again and again; yet it cannot be made otherwise by anyone at all.

sanskrit: na hi śaknoti saṃyantuṃ putraṃ kopasamanvitam tato 'haṃ preṣitas tena tava rājan hitārthinā
english: For he could not restrain his son overcome by anger; therefore I have been sent by him for your welfare, O king.

sanskrit: iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ sa rājā kurunandanaḥ paryatapyata tat pāpaṃ kṛtvā rājā mahātapāḥ
english: Hearing that terrible news, the king, delight of the Kurus, was tormented with remorse for having committed that wrong — the king of great penance.

sanskrit: taṃ ca maunavratadharaṃ śrutvā munivaraṃ tadā bhūya evābhavad rājā śokasaṃtaptamānasaḥ
english: And hearing that the great sage had been observing a vow of silence, the king's heart was again burned with grief.

sanskrit: anukrośātmatāṃ tasya śamīkasyāvadhārya tu paryatapyata bhūyo 'pi kṛtvā tat kilbiṣaṃ muneḥ
english: Recognising too the compassionate nature of Śamīka, he was tormented yet further for having committed that offence against the sage.

sanskrit: na hi mṛtyuṃ tathā rājā śrutvā vai so 'nvatapyata aśocad amaraprakhyo yathā kṛtveha karma tat
english: For the king did not grieve so much upon hearing of his impending death as he — who was like an immortal — lamented having committed that deed.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ preṣayām āsa rājā gauramukhaṃ tadā bhūyaḥ prasādaṃ bhagavān karotv iti mameti vai
english: The king then sent Gauramukha back with the message: "May the revered one be gracious to me."

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca gatamātre vai rājā gauramukhe tadā mantribhir mantrayām āsa saha saṃvignamānasaḥ
english: And as soon as Gauramukha had departed, the king, with an agitated mind, deliberated with his ministers.

sanskrit: niścitya mantribhiś caiva sahito mantratattvavit prāsādaṃ kārayām āsa ekastambhaṃ surakṣitam
english: Having decided, together with his ministers, and being expert in the essence of counsel, he had a palace built on a single pillar, well-guarded.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃ ca vidadhe tatra bhiṣajaś cauṣadhāni ca brāhmaṇān siddhamantrāṃś ca sarvato vai nyaveśayat
english: He stationed guards there, as well as physicians with medicines, and brahmins accomplished in mantras, on all sides.

sanskrit: rājakāryāṇi tatrasthaḥ sarvāṇy evākaroc ca saḥ mantribhiḥ saha dharmajñaḥ samantāt parirakṣitaḥ
english: Residing there, he conducted all affairs of state, learned in dharma, and guarded on all sides together with his ministers.

sanskrit: prāpte tu divase tasmin saptame dvijasattama kāśyapo 'bhyāgamad vidvāṃs taṃ rājānaṃ cikitsitum
english: But on the seventh day arriving, O best of brahmins, the learned Kāśyapa came to treat that king.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ hi tena tad abhūd adya taṃ rājasattamam takṣakaḥ pannagaśreṣṭho neṣyate yamasādanam
english: For it had come to his hearing that today Takṣaka, foremost of serpents, would conduct that best of kings to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: taṃ daṣṭaṃ pannagendreṇa kariṣye 'ham apajvaram tatra me 'rthaś ca dharmaś ca bhaviteti vicintayan
english: Thinking to himself: "I shall cure him after he is bitten by the lord of serpents — in that I shall find both profit and merit," he went forth.

sanskrit: taṃ dadarśa sa nāgendras takṣakaḥ kāśyapaṃ pathi gacchantam ekamanasaṃ dvijo bhūtvā vayotigaḥ
english: But the king of serpents Takṣaka saw Kāśyapa going along the road with single-pointed mind, and assuming the form of a brahmin of advanced age,

sanskrit: tam abravīt pannagendraḥ kāśyapaṃ munipuṃgavam kva bhavāṃs tvarito yāti kiṃ ca kāryaṃ cikīrṣati
english: the lord of serpents addressed Kāśyapa, foremost of sages: "Where does the venerable one hasten, and what task does he wish to accomplish?"

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca nṛpaṃ kurukulotpannaṃ parikṣitam ariṃdamam takṣakaḥ pannagaśreṣṭhas tejasādya pradhakṣyati
english: Kāśyapa said: Takṣaka, foremost of serpents, will today burn with his blazing power the king Parīkṣit, born of the Kuru lineage, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: taṃ daṣṭaṃ pannagendreṇa tenāgnisamatejasā pāṇḍavānāṃ kulakaraṃ rājānam amitaujasam gacchāmi saumya tvaritaṃ sadyaḥ kartum apajvaram
english: Him, bitten by that lord of serpents whose energy equals fire, that king of boundless might, the upholder of the Pāṇḍava lineage — I go, dear one, in haste to cure forthwith.

sanskrit: takṣaka uvāca ahaṃ sa takṣako brahmaṃs taṃ dhakṣyāmi mahīpatim nivartasva na śaktas tvaṃ mayā daṣṭaṃ cikitsitum
english: Takṣaka said: I am that Takṣaka, O brahmin; I shall burn that lord of the earth. Turn back — you are not able to cure one bitten by me.

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca ahaṃ taṃ nṛpatiṃ nāga tvayā daṣṭam apajvaram kariṣya iti me buddhir vidyābalam upāśritaḥ
english: Kāśyapa said: O serpent, it is my firm conviction that I shall cure that king after he has been bitten by you, relying on the power of my knowledge.

sanskrit: takṣaka uvāca daṣṭaṃ yadi mayeha tvaṃ śaktaḥ kiṃ cic cikitsitum tato vṛkṣaṃ mayā daṣṭam imaṃ jīvaya kāśyapa
english: Takṣaka said: If you are able to cure one bitten by me here, then revive this tree that I have bitten, O Kāśyapa.

sanskrit: paraṃ mantrabalaṃ yat te tad darśaya yatasva ca nyagrodham enaṃ dhakṣyāmi paśyatas te dvijottama
english: Display the utmost power of your mantras and exert yourself; I shall burn this banyan tree before your eyes, O foremost of brahmins.

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca daśa nāgendra vṛkṣaṃ tvaṃ yam enam abhimanyase aham enaṃ tvayā daṣṭaṃ jīvayiṣye bhujaṃgama
english: Kāśyapa said: Bite, O king of serpents, whatever tree you have in mind; I shall revive it after you have bitten it, O serpent.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktaḥ sa nāgendraḥ kāśyapena mahātmanā adaśad vṛkṣam abhyetya nyagrodhaṃ pannagottamaḥ
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Kāśyapa, that foremost of serpents, the lord of serpents, approached and bit a banyan tree.

sanskrit: sa vṛkṣas tena daṣṭaḥ san sadya eva mahādyute āśīviṣaviṣopetaḥ prajajvāla samantataḥ
english: That tree, bitten by him of great brilliance, immediately burst into flames on all sides, suffused with the venom of the poison-fanged serpent.

sanskrit: taṃ dagdhvā sa nagaṃ nāgaḥ kāśyapaṃ punar abravīt kuru yatnaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha jīvayainaṃ vanaspatim
english: Having burned that tree, the serpent again addressed Kāśyapa: "Make the effort, O best of brahmins; revive this lord of the forest."

sanskrit: bhasmībhūtaṃ tato vṛkṣaṃ pannagendrasya tejasā bhasma sarvaṃ samāhṛtya kāśyapo vākyam abravīt
english: Then, the tree having been reduced to ash by the power of the king of serpents, Kāśyapa gathered all the ash and spoke these words:

sanskrit: vidyābalaṃ pannagendra paśya me 'smin vanaspatau ahaṃ saṃjīvayāmy enaṃ paśyatas te bhujaṃgama
english: "Behold the power of my knowledge upon this lord of the forest, O king of serpents; I shall revive it before your eyes, O serpent."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān vidvān kāśyapo dvijasattamaḥ bhasmarāśīkṛtaṃ vṛkṣaṃ vidyayā samajīvayat
english: Then that blessed and learned Kāśyapa, best of brahmins, revived the tree that had been reduced to a heap of ash, by means of his knowledge.

sanskrit: aṅkuraṃ taṃ sa kṛtavāṃs tataḥ parṇadvayānvitam palāśinaṃ śākhinaṃ ca tathā viṭapinaṃ punaḥ
english: He caused it first to sprout, then to bear two leaves, then to put forth foliage and branches, and then to become a full tree once again.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jīvitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ kāśyapena mahātmanā uvāca takṣako brahmann etad atyadbhutaṃ tvayi
english: Seeing the tree restored to life by the great-souled Kāśyapa, Takṣaka said: "O brahmin, this is exceedingly wondrous in you.

sanskrit: viprendra yad viṣaṃ hanyā mama vā madvidhasya vā kaṃ tvam artham abhiprepsur yāsi tatra tapodhana
english: O lord of brahmins, you who could neutralise the venom of one like me — what purpose do you seek to gain by going there, O treasury of austerity?

sanskrit: yat te 'bhilaṣitaṃ prāptuṃ phalaṃ tasmān nṛpottamāt aham eva pradāsyāmi tat te yady api durlabham
english: Whatever fruit you desire to obtain from that best of kings, I myself will give you that, even if it be difficult to obtain.

sanskrit: vipraśāpābhibhūte ca kṣīṇāyuṣi narādhipe ghaṭamānasya te vipra siddhiḥ saṃśayitā bhavet
english: For in the case of a king whose life is waning, overwhelmed by a brahmin's curse, even your best efforts may meet with uncertain success, O brahmin.

sanskrit: tato yaśaḥ pradīptaṃ te triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam viraśmir iva gharmāṃśur antardhānam ito vrajet
english: And then your fame, blazing and renowned throughout the three worlds, would vanish from here like a sunbeam robbed of its rays.

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca dhanārthī yāmy ahaṃ tatra tan me ditsa bhujaṃgama tato 'haṃ vinivartiṣye gṛhāyoragasattama
english: Kāśyapa said: I go there in desire of wealth — give me that, O serpent; then I shall return home, O best of serpents.

sanskrit: takṣaka uvāca yāvad dhanaṃ prārthayase tasmād rājñas tato 'dhikam ahaṃ te 'dya pradāsyāmi nivartasva dvijottama
english: Takṣaka said: I will give you today more than whatever wealth you would seek from that king — turn back, O foremost of brahmins.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca takṣakasya vacaḥ śrutvā kāśyapo dvijasattamaḥ pradadhyau sumahātejā rājānaṃ prati buddhimān
english: The Sūta said: Hearing the words of Takṣaka, that brilliant and wise Kāśyapa, best of brahmins, reflected deeply about the king.
